analysis:
Examined all nine batch analyses and all replayed source/metadata; replay omits 61 of 72 reviewed source units, so it cannot independently validate every local conclusion. No concrete regression is established by the available evidence.

Replayed changes introduce selected-model recovery and adoption withdrawal. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 awaits recovery before authorization supervision; ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift:1153,1222 makes retries due after unloading; Autopilot/ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:22 includes recovery in the preload busy fence. Autopilot/ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift:25-33 protects selected/pinned models and holds and bounds release by delay, dwell and lease; lines 41-48 withdraw adoption and update capacity/heartbeat. These are availability-policy changes relevant to A-018, TB-007 and T-059, not demonstrated authorization or encryption bypasses. Saved configuration refresh at ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:80 does not itself apply serving selection.

Remaining material review: inspect ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift to establish that the capacity call dispatches bounded work rather than delaying authorization supervision (T-053/T-057), and that eviction rechecks, request admission, selection changes and add-on cancellation prevent stale victim retirement or post-hold residency publication. Documentation at docs/architecture/addon-hold.md:67-70 promises that fence; cooperative cancellation tests alone do not prove native-load enforcement. Verify withdrawn adoptions cannot accept new requests while existing work drains.

The analyses report bounded shutdown teardown at ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift:77-97 and recovery cancellation at ProviderLoop+Serve.swift:565. Those sources are omitted from replay. Confirm unfinished native retirement remains safely owned, cache clearing is safe, and successful shutdown actually terminates the credential-holding process before logout/restart (A-008, T-053, T-028). No supplied change establishes weakened T-041 cache scope, encryption, TTL or artifact binding; reload paths should retain existing verified-model admission. Human review of these unresolved lifecycle contracts is needed, not a finding based on missing source.
